2F.20 The Law of God will bring curses and punishment if disobeyed.

precepts.text: Christ said fear not them that kill the body, but fear him which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; five sparrows are sold for two farthings, yet not one is forgotten before God, and the very hairs of your head are numbered. That is how much power the Most High holds.
precepts.point: This shows the power of the Most High over the animals: he can command the ravens to bring a man food if it be his will, just as he did Elijah.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

precepts.why:
Christ said, “Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.” Instead, “Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.”

“Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God? But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.” That is how much power the Most High holds. Not one bird is forgotten before him, and he has command over them all.

So when the word of the Lord sent Elijah to hide by the brook Cherith, he could say, “I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.” And “the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening”. The Most High has power over the animals, and he can command the ravens to bring a man food if it be his will. “Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.”

precepts.text: Let every one so love his wife even as himself, and the wife see that she reverence her husband; that reverence goes into the honor of feeding the man first, just as the widow did.
precepts.point: The instruction to feed the man of God first is a precept: the man eats first. Sisters must trust in the Lord when he tells them to reverence their husbands and be submissive in all things, and not lean to their own understanding.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

precepts.why:
“Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” That reverence goes into the honor of feeding the man first, just as the widow did.

The widow of Zarephath had only “an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse”, and was gathering two sticks to dress a last meal for herself and her son, “that we may eat it, and die.” Elijah told her, “make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.” The man of God eats first. That is a precept.

She trusted and obeyed, “and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days. And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail”. For trusting in the Lord and obeying, she was sustained.

So sisters must trust in the Lord when he tells them to reverence their husbands and be submissive in all things, and not lean to their own understanding.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

precepts.why:
“Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble. He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.”

The widow’s son fell sick, “and his sickness was so sore, that there was no breath left in him.” A man’s life is short and full of trouble, and it can be cut down like a flower. The widow took it that the child was paying for her sins: “art thou come unto me to call my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son?”

But how long a man lives is not his own to decide, nor the grieving mother’s. That rests with the Most High, as the verses that follow show.

precepts.text: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee; thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass. When the appointed day comes a man cannot pass it, but this child's day had not yet come.
precepts.point: All praises that Elijah was there to call upon the Lord, for it was not the young man's time to go. A man's days are determined and appointed, and he cannot pass the bound the Most High has set; because it was not the child's time, the Lord let his soul return.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

precepts.why:
“Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass”. A man’s days are determined and appointed. When the appointed day comes, a man cannot pass it.

But this child’s day had not yet come. Elijah carried him up into the loft, laid him on his own bed, stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried, “O Lord my God, I pray thee, let this child’s soul come into him again. And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.” Because it was not the child’s time, the Lord let his soul return.

All praises that Elijah was there to call upon the Lord. And the widow said, “Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.”

points: Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab that as the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom he stands, there shall not be dew nor rain these years but according to his word. Elijah prayed and it was no rain.
The teaching opens by framing the whole session on the power of the Most High: he has power over everything, the animals and all creation, and he set that power on display through his prophet.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

points: The word of the Lord sent Elijah eastward to hide by the brook Cherith before Jordan, and there he drank of the brook and the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning and in the evening.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

points: The brook dried up for want of rain, and the Lord sent Elijah all the way across the land to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon on the coast, where he had commanded a widow woman to sustain him. From the east side by Jordan to the west by Sidon was a hard walk of a Sabbath day's journey or more, with no water anywhere.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

points: Coming to the gate, Elijah asked the widow for water and a morsel of bread, and she answered that she had but a handful of meal in a barrel and a little oil in a cruise, gathering two sticks to dress a last meal for herself and her son that they might eat it and die.

Elijah told her to make him a little cake first and after that for herself and her son, for the Lord God of Israel said the barrel of meal would not waste nor the cruise of oil fail until the day the Lord sent rain. She obeyed, and she and Elijah and her house did eat many days. For trusting in the Lord and obeying, she was sustained.

The instruction to feed the man of God first is a precept: the man eats first. Sisters must trust in the Lord when he tells them to reverence their husbands and be submissive in all things, and not lean to their own understanding.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

points: After these things the widow's son fell sick, and his sickness was so sore that there was no breath left in him. She said unto Elijah, Art thou come to call my sin to remembrance and to slay my son? Her thought was that the child was paying for the parent's sins.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

points: Elijah took the child up to the loft, laid him on his own bed, and cried unto the Lord, stretching himself upon the child three times and praying that the child's soul come into him again. The Lord heard the voice of Elijah, and the soul of the child came into him again and he revived.

All praises that Elijah was there to call upon the Lord, for it was not the young man's time to go. A man's days are determined and appointed, and he cannot pass the bound the Most High has set; because it was not the child's time, the Lord let his soul return.

note.label: 1 Kings 17: The Word of the Lord in Elijah's Mouth Is Truth

points: Elijah delivered the living child to his mother, and she said, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.
